clue.text: One gets more lit up each year

definitions.text: One gets more lit up each year

parts.words: One gets more lit up each year
parts.note: a festive bake whose candles grow by one with every passing year, so more is lit up annually

explanation.surface: Someone who gets drunker with every passing year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lit up' suggests drunkenness; it is really candles lit on the bake, one more each year.
explanation.definitionFit: The celebratory cake bears one candle per year of age, so each year more candles are lit.

clue.text: Boy sailor on good stretch of river in oz

parts.note: Bill is a boy's name
AB, able seaman, is the usual sailor

explanation.surface: A lad who went to sea goes on to a fine stretch of river in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oz' is slang for Australia, where the word comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian English it is a backwater or cut-off pool left by a river that has changed course.

clue.text: Part of mountain journey across Germany's frontier

indicators.note: the trip word is laid across the letter, which therefore sits inside it

parts.note: a ride is a journey

indicators.note: the frontier of a word is its leading edge, its first letter

explanation.surface: A trip across the German border takes in part of a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow crest running along a mountain is one of its parts.

clue.text: Sounding rough — not a runner in the 3.10?

indicators.note: the word for rough is to be heard rather than spelt, giving a different word

parts.note: a rough voice is hoarse

explanation.surface: A croaky voice, and a horse scratched from the ten-past-three race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' tells you the rough-sounding word itself is not what you write: you write the racehorse that sounds the same. The 3.10 is a race time at the races.
explanation.definitionFit: Races are known by their start times, and the competitors in them are horses.

clue.text: Bit of food that could give eater pips

indicators.note: the letters given could be reshuffled to produce something else

explanation.surface: A morsel that might make a diner spit out pips.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter or small snack is served to whet the appetite before a meal.

clue.text: Character in Athens wants cradle rocked — must pay for this?

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a character used in Athens

indicators.note: a rocked cradle is shaken about, so its letters move

explanation.surface: A Greek wants the cradle rocked, and must pay someone to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: Working parents must pay nurseries or minders for looking after their young.

clue.text: Pussy makes a pool!

explanation.surface: A cat produces a puddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet name for a cat, and a shared fund of money, as in a card game's pot.

clue.text: Getting together before a possible match?

definitions.text: Getting together before a possible match?

parts.words: Getting together before a possible match?
parts.note: a couple living together before a possible marriage, not players meeting before a game

explanation.surface: Teams meeting before a game might be played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests sport; here it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Living together as partners often precedes, and may lead to, a wedding.

clue.text: Moved with difficulty, not having front bit lubricated

indicators.note: the word drops its leading letter, its front bit

parts.note: to toil is to move laboriously

explanation.surface: Something without its front piece moved stiffly until greased.
explanation.definitionFit: Greased with oil, as a stiff hinge is.

clue.text: Agent isn't man to be given a new coat

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't
Ed is a man's name

explanation.surface: A salesman is not the man to be handed a new jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Painted again, with a fresh coat of paint.

clue.text: The value of money for the Methodist church maybe

explanation.surface: What the Methodists are worth in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: The face value of a note or coin, and a branch of the Christian church, of which Methodism is one.

clue.text: Shock at having to bypass complex path with soldiers

indicators.note: the first word goes round the others, as a bypass circles a town

parts.note: taken as written
a maze is a complex network of paths
men are soldiers in the ranks

explanation.surface: Troops are startled at having to go round a tangled route.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishment is the feeling of being shocked or overwhelmed by surprise.

clue.text: Senior member with desire to follow party

indicators.note: the desire word comes after the party word

parts.note: a do is a party
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: An elder statesman keen to follow the party line.
explanation.definitionFit: The most senior or respected member of a group or profession.

clue.text: Features on map showing nasty shore mist

indicators.note: a nasty mist suggests the words are in a bad state and scrambled

explanation.surface: A weather chart reveals an unpleasant sea fret along the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines on a weather map joining places with equal temperature.

clue.text: Shouting 'hello' is silly manner on phone

indicators.note: one piece is placed on top of the other in the down entry
said in a silly manner, the greeting comes out jumbled

parts.note: to ring is to phone

explanation.surface: Bawling a greeting is a foolish way to behave on the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly manner' scrambles HELLO into HOLLE, then 'on' sets it above RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Yelling or calling out loudly, an informal word for crying out.

clue.text: Tries to participate in proper practice

indicators.note: one word takes part within the other, sitting inside it

parts.note: real means genuine or proper
a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to take part in a genuine training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' is the legal sense: a court hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A practice run of a play or performance before the real thing.

clue.text: A smile across the ship

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly

explanation.surface: A grin spreading across the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical term for at right angles to a vessel's length, level with its middle.

clue.text: High-spirited Rex ate bun excitedly

indicators.note: eating excitedly suggests the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Rex wolfs down a bun in high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of energy and cheerful enthusiasm.

clue.text: Financial backer offers obsolete coin

explanation.surface: An investor hands over an old coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy investor funding a theatrical show, and an old English gold piece stamped with St Michael.

clue.text: Columbine's companion is a rugger player

explanation.surface: Columbine's friend turns out for a rugby side.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbine and her lover are pantomime characters; Harlequins is a London rugby union club.
explanation.definitionFit: The masked clown who courts Columbine in pantomime, and a member of the Harlequins rugby club.

clue.text: Little woman is first to have affair

indicators.note: the word is comes first, ahead of the woman

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name, a short form of Susan

explanation.surface: A small woman is the first to start a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affair' is not romantic here: it means a matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter or point in question, as in the business at hand.

clue.text: Loose stones making a barrier mostly

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter

parts.note: a screen is a barrier or partition

explanation.surface: Loose rocks heaped up to form most of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Broken rock fragments on a mountain slope.

clue.text: Several people intended, we hear, to get a vegetable patch

indicators.note: the words are as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: a lot meant: many people intended it

explanation.surface: Many folk had in mind getting a plot to grow vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented plot of land for growing vegetables, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rented strip of ground where people cultivate produce.

clue.text: There's rope, look, around donkey

indicators.note: the look word goes around the animal

parts.note: lo is an old word for look
an ass is a donkey

explanation.surface: Someone sees a rope looped round a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a running noose, used by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: Part of body that can make you t-tall

parts.note: high means tall

explanation.surface: A body part that might make you stammer about being tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 't-tall' is a stammered tall: a T before a word for tall.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper part of the leg between hip and knee.

clue.text: Susan is bothered about Catholic youth pining away

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go about the abbreviation
bothered means flustered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Susan is upset about a young Catholic lovesick and wasting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' turns SUSAN IS into NA ISSUS, which goes 'about' RC. In Greek myth the youth pined away for his own reflection.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical youth who fell for his reflection and wasted away, becoming a flower.

clue.text: Insect has been caught by him — a goner!

indicators.note: the letters are caught within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An insect is caught by a man and that is the end of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The final adult stage of an insect after metamorphosis.

clue.text: Black one on cowboy? Somehow not gallant, he!

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: A cowboy in a black hat is no gallant, so he must be the villain.
explanation.walkthrough: In westerns the villain wears a black hat, worn on a cowboy's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall wide-brimmed hat typical of cowboys, perhaps black.
